unharnessed.meaning: Every step and quantity survives: the fifteen-minute boil, "three-quarters of a pound of fat salt pork", "a quarter-inch slice", cuts "every half inch, making the cuts an inch deep", the salt/molasses/sugar mix, "six or eight hours", the mustard tip, the lard bucket. "some poor bugger broke the bean pot" is colour on 'the broken bean-pot'.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "Snags" for sausages, "go in the bin", "chuck the bean water outside", "low and slow", "go down easier on the guts" for 'more easily digested', "lard bucket" for 'lard pail'.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Aussie cook talking: "Chuck 'em in the frying pan", "whack it in the bottom of the bean pot", "Lid on the bean pot, into the oven".
unharnessed.register: Solidly Aussie with "bloody good" and "poor bugger" inside vulgarity 2, but closer to a chatty kitchen voice than a full level-5 yarn; long stretches are plain instructions ("Mix one tablespoon salt, one tablespoon molasses and three tablespoons sugar").
unharnessed.tone: Stays a practical recipe with a little wry humour, as the original does with the lard pail.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "Best way to tell is to grab a few beans on the tip of a spoon and blow on 'em; if they're done, the skins'll split."
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("chuck", "whack", "Tip", "Score"), though "bloody good" appears twice.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the 1896 recipes, keeping the spoon-blowing test and the lard-pail punchline.

yarn.meaning: All steps and quantities kept ("three-quarters of a pound", "every half an inch", "six or eight hours", mustard, lard bucket). Small additions: "toss out the duds" elaborates 'pick over'; "to catch the drips" adds a purpose the original does not state; "So don't sweat it if ya haven't got the proper pot." is colour.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "Come sparrow's fart" for 'In morning', "the bean pot was cactus" for broken, "just as beaut a feed of beans", "go down a lot easier on the guts", "brown and crackly".
yarn.authenticity: A real Aussie voice: "Bung 'em in the fryin' pan", "keep the water under the boil, mind", "Heaps of people reckon".
yarn.register: Full level-5 retelling with dropped g's, "sparrow's fart", "cactus" and "bloody good", within vulgarity 2.
yarn.tone: Still a practical recipe, told with a grin; the lard-bucket joke lands and the reassurance "don't sweat it" fits.
yarn.flow: Reads naturally: "Lid on the bean pot, into the oven, and bake it low and slow for six or eight hours."
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the original recipes, with the blowing test and the lard pail intact.

engine.meaning: The original text is mostly left intact, so the steps survive, but "beans thus tested must, too bloody right, be chucked away" and "Equally beaut beans" shift sense slightly.
engine.sense: Wrong-sense swaps: "too bloody right" for 'of course' (it means 'absolutely agreed'), "Equally beaut beans", "dead beaut when baked".
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: interjections bolted on ("Bugger me, snags", "Mind ya, Pierce each snag", "Jeez Louise, put in frying-pan", "Struth, Boston Baked Beans", "Crikey, put beans in pot", "Too easy.") onto Victorian recipe prose.
engine.register: Level 5 asked, but the body is untranslated ("Scald rind of three-fourths pound fat salt pork, scrape, remove one-fourth inch slice"), with slang sprinkled on.
engine.tone: The recipe's plainness is broken by exclamations like "Jeez Louise," that make it a parody.
engine.flow: Jarring joins: "Mind ya, Pierce each snag", "Now, Snags are often broiled", "small top'n bulgin' sides", "'ave gained's been attributed".
engine.variety: Leans on the same opener tics ("Well,", "Now,", "Crikey,") and "beaut".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original because it mostly is the original, but turned into a gag reel.

summaries.unharnessed: Natural, accurate and easy to follow; a touch lighter than the full level-5 yarn asked for.
summaries.yarn: A natural, full-strength Aussie retelling that keeps every step; only tiny added detail.
summaries.engine: The original with interjections and dropped g's bolted on; untranslated, jarring and well short of level 5.
